Subject: Success yardstick & acceptance checklist — draft MAP for CareVast pilot

Hi Lena —

Thanks again for the time today. Attached is our initial mutual action plan (MAP) draft and a compact acceptance checklist focused on the pilot objectives we discussed. High-level asks:

- Can you confirm the top 3 success yardsticks for the pilot from CareVast's perspective (accuracy, latency, and integration ease are my guess).
- Please flag any compliance evidence you need (SOC 2 artifacts, data residency statements).
- We propose a 4-week evaluation window with a go/no-go decision on week 5; open to adjusting if you need a longer runway.

Summary of proposed acceptance tests (short):
1) Functional: end-to-end generation accuracy on 200 sampled prompts (target > 88% concordance with golden set).
2) Performance: P95 infer latency < 450ms for 512-token requests under test traffic (20 concurrent sessions).
3) Resilience: zero unplanned downtime and automatic fallback to a smaller model under resource pressure.
4) Security: encrypted-at-rest verification and evidence of KMS key usage for any private deployment.

Next steps I suggest:
- You review the attached MAP-draft-CareVast-v1.pdf and note edits in-line.
- Karthik will send a short acceptance-tests spreadsheet with test owners and pass/fail thresholds.
- We align on the decision sprint dates by Friday.

I attached the MAP draft and a one-sheet acceptance checklist. If this looks good, I can convert to a mutual tracker in HubSpot and link back to your procurement contact.

Best,

Appreciate the draft. A few quick notes from procurement and the analytics team:
- CareVast's priority yardsticks are (1) extraction accuracy for clinical fields (target: >90% F1 on selected set), (2) end-to-end throughput at peak (ability to sustain 35rps with P95 < 600ms), and (3) reproducible results between runs (concordance >= 95%).
- We will need SOC 2 Type II report and a short data retention policy statement before we sign the MAP. Can you point to where those live?

Also looping in our security counterparty (procurement@carevast.com) for artifacts. If you can update the acceptance tests spreadsheet to reflect clinical F1 and concordance metrics, that would help.

Thanks Lena — good clarity. Per your asks, I pushed a focused acceptance-tests spreadsheet into the Drive link (see related_links) and pasted a short executable plan below.

-- Acceptance tests (executable):
A) Clinical extraction accuracy (owner: CareVast analytics / validation):
  - Test: Run 200 labeled clinical records through the pipeline; compute F1; target >= 90% (pass), 85-90% (conditional pass with remediation), <85% (fail).
  - Evidence: results CSV + scoring notebook saved to shared Drive folder.

B) Concordance (owner: Redwood engineering):
  - Test: Re-run the same 200 prompts with identical seeds/config 5x across different nodes; compute pairwise agreement; target >= 95%.
  - Evidence: pairwise delta report + configuration snapshot.

C) Performance & throughput (owner: Redwood infra):
  - Test: Synthetic load test to 35rps sustained for 15 minutes with a 512-token median; metrics: P50, P95, P99.
  - Pass: P95 < 600ms; Conditional: 600-800ms with pipeline tuning plan; Fail: >800ms.

D) Security/compliance (owner: CareVast security + Redwood security):
  - Test: Provide SOC 2 link, KMS key usage screenshots, and data-residency confirmation.

-- Exit gates (hard stop):
1) Failure of security evidence or failure to provide SOC 2 within the agreed window.
2) Two consecutive performance load tests with P95 > 800ms.
3) Clinical extraction F1 < 85% after two remediation attempts.

If those exit gates are acceptable we can embed them into the MAP doc and make them sign-off items in HubSpot. Priyom — I left notes on owners and estimated effort per test in the spreadsheet.

-Karthik
VP, Solutions | Redwood Inference
